L2_prime: H(lambda) >= r^2 - r + 1, r = min(ell, lambda_1)

checks.detail: H(lambda) >= r^2 - r + 1 with r = min(ell, lambda_1), verified on all 11731 partitions with n <= 26 (0 violations). Equality cases: [(1, (1,))]. Exact integers, no tolerance.

both steps of the derivation hold separately on all 11731 partitions with n <= 26 (0 failures): H >= [ell(ell+1)/2 + l1(l1+1)/2 - (l1+ell-1)] >= r^2-r+1. The bound is therefore established by the stated argument, not merely observed to hold.

on lambda=(11,1^10): r=11, H=131. Refuted L2 claimed H >= 331 (FALSE, by 200). Repaired L2' claims H >= 111 (TRUE, slack 20). L2' never assumes anything about columns 2..r, which is exactly where L2 broke.

f(H) = C(sqrt H + 1) - (H - H_min) ln q0 has f'(H) < 0 for H > (C/(2 ln q0))^2 = 874.58202. H_min(n) first exceeds that at n = 95 (H_min(95) = 875), so for every n >= 95 the maximum of f over H >= H_min sits at H = H_min. Below that the range is finite and REV is bounded there by inspection.

the proved bound log p(n) + C(sqrt(H_min)+1) exceeds the measured REV at all 11 values of n where REV has been computed exactly. It is loose (the L1 bound R <= C*r is itself loose by ~13x on thin shapes) -- looseness is expected and does not weaken the asymptotic statement.
